message.content:
I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$8,920 total).

**Summary:** Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 report (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024, released Oct 31) showed quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year FY2024 results of $391.0B in net sales, $93.7B in net income, and $6.08 diluted EPS — the latter depressed by a one-time $10.2B income tax charge — alongside very strong $118.3B in operating cash flow, confirming the business remains highly cash-generative. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual rollout of Apple Intelligence, meaning expectations are moderate rather than euphoric, which I viewed as a reasonable entry point rather than a reason to avoid the name. With the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 40 shares at $223.00 — a limit essentially at market, ~$8,920 notional, comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, buying only (no cash withdrawn), and within the AAPL/MSFT-only mandate. The order filled at $223.00, leaving the account with the new AAPL position plus the existing 100 MSFT shares and remaining cash.
message.reasoning: Order filled at 223.00, 40 shares = $8,920, within $10k per order and $20k total. Summarize.
